title: Kewan Lacy injury: Ole Miss star RB expected to return for Week 6 game vs. Vanderbilt - CBS Sports
description: The Rebels will get a key piece back ahead of their Week 6 game against Vandy
body:
The Rebels will get a key piece back ahead of their Week 6 game against Vandy
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 5, 2026

    3:40 pm ET

            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Ole Miss had a well-timed bye week in Week 5 to reset after an emotional early-season rollercoaster saw them beat Lane Kiffin and LSU before traveling to Gainesville, where they were dominated by Florida. As the Rebels come out of their bye week with a Week 6 game in Nashville against Vanderbilt, they got some good news with the expected return of star running back Kewan Lacy. Lacy left the Rebels win over LSU in the first half with an undisclosed injury and was unable to play in the loss to Florida. He's expected back against Vanderbilt after taking advantage of the bye week to get healthy. "Obviously [Lacy] rested all last week," Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said in his Monday press conference. "Was good for a solid week, not practicing. Practiced last night, came back. Did individual, did some team sessions. A lot of that was non-contact last week. Fully anticipate having him this week."
Lacy's return a much-needed addition to offenseThe Ole Miss run game struggled in Lacy's absence, as backups JT Lindsey and Makhi Frazier combined for 93 yards on 23 carries across the two games after Lacy's injury. Against Florida, star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss ended up the team's leading rusher with 44 yards and two touchdowns on the ground, and he will be glad to have his star running back alongside him in the backfield again this week in Nashville. Lacy has 191 rushing yards and four touchdowns this season on 39 carries, coming off a 2025 campaign in which he was the Rebels' bell cow with more than 306 carries for 1,564 yards and 24 touchdowns. Golding noted that they'll be cognizant of Lacy's workload as they work him back into the running back rotation, noting Lacy's "not going to take the toll of 40 or 50 snaps." 
The Ole Miss rushing attack, even with Lacy, has not been as dynamic in 2026, leaning more on Chambliss' arm early in the season. But they'd like to have a more balanced attack and will hope Lacy's return provides that going forward.

title: High stakes, pressure bring out best in Tom Kim, Adrian Meronk over wild weekend - CBS Sports
description: From the FedEx Cup Fall slate on the PGA Tour all the way to the Asian Games, this weekend in golf was not one to
body:
From the FedEx Cup Fall slate on the PGA Tour all the way to the Asian Games, this weekend in golf was not one to miss
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Society continues to push past upper limits. More, more, more. It is the only word that seems universal in 2026, when no one can agree on how anything should be done. Everyone needs more, though, and suppliers are more than happy to produce it for consumers. At the grocery store, suddenly, alongside regular options, are versions with more protein or more fiber. The maxxing trend has been taken to the exxtreme. Does one actually need 10 additional grams of protein in their strawberry Pop-Tarts? Is that what will lead you to hit your goals?It could be! Who am I to say otherwise?This conversation is not exclusive to grocery store aisles, of course. It is weighed in world affairs, financial sectors, entertainment and obviously sports. It is a constant barrage from every corner of life, and it is this current state of society that made this weekend in golf refreshing to watch unfold.Professional golf has never had a more problem, unless we are discussing commercial load or pace of play. This past weekend had the U.S. Mid-Amateur Championship (sure, a stretch of the "professional" designator) and tournaments on the DP World Tour, Korn Ferry Tour, PGA Tour and LPGA, as well as the Asian Games held in Japan. 
That is plenty to consume in the first weekend of October, about a month after the FedEx Cup Playoffs ended. More than enough.Tom Kim went straight from the Presidents Cup in Chicago to the Asian Games in Kasugai, Aichi, Japan. The games represented one of two remaining opportunities he had to earn an exemption from mandatory military service in his home country, South Korea.Kim had to win a gold medal in either the individual competition or the team portion of the event. If he did not, his last remaining chance would be the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, where a medal of any color would lead to an exemption. No more after that.
Two at-bats to avoid 21 months in the military. A commitment that has derailed PGA Tour players from South Korea in the past. That's all Kim had after falling short in the 2024 Olympics in Paris. The 24-year-old got what he came for. A final-round 64 was enough to convert his one-stroke lead at the 54-hole mark into a three-stroke victory by tournament's end."At a [PGA Tour] event, it is not as if you would feel tension every day from Thursday to Sunday," Kim said. "But this week, I was nervous from start to finish."
At the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship on the DP World Tour, Adrian Meronk -- once a significant signing for LIV Golf's Cleeks GC -- completed what may have been the most important final round of his career. Arriving in St. Andrews No. 141 in the Race to Dubai standings, Meronk was in need of something to secure playing privileges somewhere else in 2027 with his home league's status in flux.With time running out and the season coming to a close, Meronk closed his front nine with a birdie while overnight leader Casey Jarvis slipped up on the Old Course's short par 4. The two exchanged bogeys on the Road Hole a couple of hours later, leaving the 33-year-old from Poland with a two-stroke edge by the time the final putt dropped.Now a five-time winner on the DP World Tour, Meronk has a card next year on the same circuit where he claimed Player of the Year honors over Rory McIlroy in 2023.
It is players like McIlroy that Austin Smotherman will see plenty of the next two seasons. In his 100th start on the PGA Tour, Smotherman put together a record-setting performance at the Bank of Utah Championship to claim his first career victory by two strokes over Doug Ghim.Smotherman bounced back from an ugly double bogey from the middle of the fairway on No. 13 on Sunday with three birdies in his final five holes to secure his maiden trip to the winner's circle. The win pushes the 32-year-old's name from No. 79 in the FedEx Cup Fall standings to No. 51, all but securing spots in the field for Smotherman in the first two signature events of 2027.More importantly, Smotherman locks up his place in the PGA Tour Championship Series in 2028, as exemptions earned this season will still carry weight when the tour's new competitive structure arrives.
The stakes on the DP World Tour and PGA Tour were not as severe as those Kim faced -- how could they be? -- but they were still present, and it is because these events all had something in common that their societal counterparts will never have ...Looming finality.An end line that can be seen, which in turn raises the stakes. It is under these conditions that the best comes out, especially in a sport such as golf. Players are able to rise to the occasion. They are able to dig deep and muster up the strength they might not even know they possess to seize the moment. They are able to overcome the nerves, the doubts and the lack of additional chances down the pipeline to take what is out in front of them right then and now.
By staring down the barrel of less, they are able to get more out of themselves than they could ever imagine.

title: NFL reviewing heated exchange between referee, Vikings' Eric Wilson - CBS Sports
description: The league reviewed two separate incidents involving a pla
body:
The league reviewed two separate incidents involving a player and an official during Week 4
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        The NFL suspended referee Adrian Hill one game for "unprofessional conduct" toward Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson in Week 4. The ruling came after the league reviewed a play from the Vikings' 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins in which Wilson and Hill collided.Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II shoved Wilson into the referee, who then fell backward to the ground. Wilson saw the referee take the tumble and extended his arms to help him up, but instead of taking the assistance, the referee stood up under his own power and began yelling at Wilson. It appeared that the referee took exception to the inadvertent collision and blamed Wilson, while Wilson pointed at Gordon and said that it was the Dolphins player who initiated the contact.A second official stepped in to separate Wilson from the referee after they exchanged words and pointed in opposite directions. The referee appeared to be instructing Wilson to return to his side of the field.
This is not the only play involving an official and a player that raised eyebrows on Sunday. The NFL also reviewed an interaction between official Jeff Seeman and Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. McBride pleaded for a pass interference penalty, to which the official appeared to deliver a profane response. That incident prompted a response from NFL Players Association president JC Tretter and a two-game suspension for Seeman."This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter said. "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel also had a heated moment with an official over a pass interference situation. Vrabel was said to have told a down judge that he made "a f---ing terrible call," which drew an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. Vrabel called the official "a little sensitive" for issuing the flag.

title: Mike Norvell sees growth in Florida State before key stretch vs. ACC contenders - CBS Sports
description: Despite occupying one of college football's hottest seats, Norvell sees light at the end of the tunnel for the Se
body:
Despite occupying one of college football's hottest seats, Norvell sees light at the end of the tunnel for the Seminoles
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:33 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Mike Norvell noticed more pep in Florida State's step in Saturday's 31-point win over Virginia, a victory the Seminoles hope to build on in the ACC with three consecutive potential narrative-setters in the coming weeks.CBS Sports reported last month that there's a path for Norvell to keep his job, but it would be determined in part by what happens during a key stretch this month against the likes of Virginia, Louisville, Miami and Clemson. The first step is behind him after Florida State crushed Virginia, and looked good doing it."When you're at home, and it's not a secret ... we understand what everybody desires for it to look like, and there's frustrations when it doesn't," Norvell said Monday. "For us to start off the game that nobody in the stands or field wants it to look like. When you're at home, you feel it all. The energy. This is an incredible place to get to play, to get to coach, you feel the passion of our fan base."To be able to really hone in and through a couple disappointing drives ... the guys just continue to hammer away at it and I love that. That's something that's going to be needed Friday night, it's going to be needed throughout the course of the season and needed when start off, sitting there, 1-2 at beginning of the year."
No players hung their heads after the early deficit against Virginia before Florida State rattled off the game's final 38 points, highlighted by five touchdowns on the ground from quarterback Ashton Daniels.
"When you stay focused, you can stay true to yourself and continue to pour into each other, that's what I want from the team," Norvell said, acknowledging he loved the sideline momentum he felt against Virginia.Friday night's game at Louisville is a chance to snap another streak for Norvell, whose program hasn't won a true road game since beating Florida in 2023, losing 10 straight.
"When it's not looking good, you've got to feed off each and that's where I think our guys (are growing)," Norvell said.At 3-2 overall and 1-1 in the ACC, it's imperative the Seminoles finish the first half strong prior to a trip to Miami to take on the unbeaten, fourth-ranked Hurricanes on Oct. 17. The open date comes after that, leading into a home bout with Dabo Swinney and Clemson.Getting to bowl eligibility feels much more feasible with a strong performance Friday night than it would if the Seminoles take one on the chin against the Cardinals, given what's left on the slate.

title: Steve Gleason opens up on how Saints' 'Rebirth' game has kept him alive through ALS battle 20 years later - CBS Sports
description: Gleason's blocked punt was a pivotal moment for both the city of New Orleans and himself. Now, 20 years later, he
body:
Gleason's blocked punt was a pivotal moment for both the city of New Orleans and himself. Now, 20 years later, he opened up on 'Good Morning America' about his own 'rebirth'
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:40 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The parallels between Steve Gleason's legendary blocked punt, what it meant for the city of New Orleans and how it resembles his own personal struggle are chilling. A play on the football field that will forever be known as the "rebirth" of New Orleans was, in many ways, a "rebirth" for Gleason. He just did not know it at the time.Almost exactly 20 years ago, the New Orleans Saints returned to the Superdome for the first time since Hurricane Katrina devastated the city. The venue that served as a shelter for thousands during and after the storm became, once again, the home of a proud football team. A minute and a half after the opening kickoff of the Sept. 25, 2006, game against the rival Atlanta Falcons, Gleason made the most memorable play in franchise history, blocking a punt that was scooped up in the end zone. It was a play that gave the Saints and the city of New Orleans hope once again.
On Monday, the Falcons return to the Superdome to face the Saints in Week 4 of the 2026 season.  The team will honor Gleason and that 2006 squad in a 20th anniversary celebration.It will undoubtedly be a meaningful return to the Superdome for Gleason."When I roll back into that stadium, I will not only be revisiting a monument of 2006, but I will be walking into a mirror — a place that had to learn how to rise," Gleason said on "Good Morning America" on Monday. "I had to learn the same thing."
Steve Gleason's battle with ALS after football careerFive years after he made an indelible mark on New Orleans with his blocked punt, in 2011, Gleason revealed that he was diagnosed with ALS. The average life expectancy after diagnosis is about three to five years, yet Gleason is among the 10-20% of those who survive for 10 years or more."I'm still here," Gleason said on GMA. "That still surprises some people. It does not surprise me as much as it used to."Gleason uses speech synthesis technology to communicate and requires assistance to move and breathe. Still, he relishes in a "miraculous, wonderful life" and remains an active contributor to the ALS awareness movement. He became the first NFL player to win a Congressional Gold Medal in 2019 for his activism.
NFL players represent one of the populations that is at higher risk of developing ALS than the general public, Gleason said. He found community with other football players who battled or are currently battling the disease, including Chris Johnson, Tim Shaw, O.J. Brigance, Eric Stevens, and Steve Smith.What "Rebirth" means to GleasonThat game 20 years ago did not just revive the city of New Orleans. In hindsight, it was a pivotal moment in Gleason's life. It just took a few years for him to fully realize what it would mean to be a central figure in a defining moment in the city's and the football team's history."If I do not block that punt, I am another former special teams player, a has-been football guy," Gleason said. "When ALS came, I probably fade away quietly and die anonymously. That play made me visible at the exact moment this city needed a symbol. Years later, that visibility became a lifeline. So many people have told us our foundation's work saved their lives."
Last week, Gleason announced that he will release a musical album. The project combines his poetry with the instrumental talent of local musicians in New Orleans. He has already released two tracks and will continue to unveil more throughout the month of October. The songs are largely influenced by Gleason's life since his ALS diagnosis.Fittingly, the album is titled "Rebirth.""The truth I have to live with is this: The same play that helped New Orleans breathe again," Gleason said, "is a big reason I'm still breathing now."How Gleason remembers his blocked puntGleason, a special teams stalwart, ran unblocked to deflect the Falcons' punt into the end zone, where Curtis Deloatch recovered the loose ball for a touchdown. The crowd popped when Gleason made contact with the ball, rivaling that of any big play in football history. It was a cathartic moment for a city that, over the previous year, had been through misery.
For the first time in a year, New Orleans had something to cheer about."During the Falcons' first two games of the year, we noticed a lot of confusion and errors on their punt team, so we wanted to exploit that," Gleason said, recounting the preparation for that contest. "The scheme is an interior stunt where I cross from the right A gap to the left A gap. Sure enough, the Falcons had some confusion on their assignments. Because they used the slide technique, I ended up unblocked and the B gap opened up for me."At that point, there wasn't much thinking. All the film study, repetition and technique took over. The gap opened, and I knew I had a real chance. Then the ball hit my hands."The Saints had spent the past year bouncing from stadium to stadium because of the damage Hurricane Katrina had done to the Superdome. They went 3-13 in that adversity-filled campaign. Questions arose about whether the franchise would return to the Superdome or to New Orleans in general.
But after a year of repairs to the facility, the Saints made their way back to the Superdome and dominated their division rival. The blocked punt helped the Saints down the Falcons 23-3 in a game that was symbolic of New Orleans' revival as a city.In turn, a statue of that blocked punt stands outside the Superdome.

title: Caleb Williams to miss Bears' Week 5 rivalry game against Packers, Tyson Bagent set for second start - CBS Sports
description: The Bears are unbeaten without Williams in the starting lineup
body:
The Bears are unbeaten without Williams in the starting lineup
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Chicago Bears will be without quarterback Caleb Williams for at least one more game. Coach Ben Johnson said Monday on ESPN Chicago that Tyson Bagent "will be the guy" for the Week 5 rivalry game against the Green Bay Packers, which sets him up for his second consecutive start after he guided the Bears to a 23-12 win over the New York Jets on Sunday.Williams remains on the mend from a hamstring strain and is poised to miss his third consecutive game. He suffered that injury in the Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, and in his absence, both Bagent and third-string quarterback Case Keenum stepped up to keep the offense rolling. They orchestrated plenty of success in back-to-back victories.Bagent would have been in line to start against the Philadelphia Eagles in the first Williams-less game, but he spent most of Week 3 in the NFL's concussion protocol, which prompted Johnson to turn to Keenum. Now that Bagent is cleared, though, this is his offense until Williams returns. Chicago signed him to a two-year, $10 million contract extension in the offseason and regards him as a premier backup, so it was unsurprising that Johnson called his name even though Keenum was highly effective starting two games ago.Bagent completed 25 of 34 passes against the Jets and amassed 268 yards through the air. He did not account for either of the Bears' touchdowns, though, and he threw one interception. Running back Kyle Monangai did the majority of the scoring with his two trips to the end zone on the ground.
"Some good and some that I think he wants back," Johnson said of Bagent's first start of 2026. "It's a little bit of a mixed bag. The best part is how he controlled the operation. I thought we had good tempo in and out of the huddle. I thought our guys played with a lot of confidence because of how he conducted himself. He found completions. I thought he played an efficient football game."The hamstring strain Williams sustained in the Week 2 loss reportedly comes with a three-to-four-week recovery timeline, so even though the Bears initially labeled him as "week to week," there was always a real chance he would be unavailable for the NFC North battle against the Packers.
If Williams misses the full four weeks, he will also sit against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 6. That would set him up for a potential prime-time return against the New England Patriots on the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football."

title: Why Shane Beamer's future at South Carolina isn't as tenuous as it might seem - CBS Sports
description: The Gamecocks are on an eight-game SEC losing streak dating back to last season, but sources indicate that moving
body:
The Gamecocks are on an eight-game SEC losing streak dating back to last season, but sources indicate that moving on from Beamer in the near future could be too expensive
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the wake of South Carolina's 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky on Saturday -- the Gamecocks' eighth straight SEC defeat -- intel began leaking from sources close to the program that South Carolina intends to keep embattled coach Shane Beamer not just for the short term, but perhaps through the 2027 season.Despite Beamer's 12th loss to Power Four opponents in 14 tries dating back to last season, it appears the sixth-year coach's job is secure for the time being. Breaking away from Beamer now or in the near future, sources say, would not be in the university's best interest financially.  Local outlets, like The Post and Courier, and 247Sports (VIP subscription required), were reporting on the buyout costs associated with Beamer's contract after Saturday night's loss, but The State reported that a change was "highly unlikely," given the financial constraints for a school that subsidized its athletic department more than any other SEC program in the last fiscal year, giving "South Carolina athletics over $42 million in direct institutional support" to assist with keeping up in the nation's most competitive league.CBS Sports asked a high-end donor at South Carolina whether the school could afford Beamer's estimated $22.5 million buyout, and the conversation quickly shifted to the overall complexity of the issue.
In essence, there's no real appetite to make a move financially."It's so much more than stepping up to write a check," the source said.
        
            
                Hot Seat Watch: Which college football coaches have helped -- or hurt -- their job security?
                
                    John Talty                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
And this is where it gets sticky for an athletic department that would be paying a head coach a buyout, covering the remaining contracts of various assistants, and then earmarking more funds for a brand-new staff.This is where the $22.5 million number swells to at least $40 million, one source estimated. There are also the initial phases of the Williams-Brice Stadium renovation project that soak up an estimated $350 million.The university's paying for this through various self-funding channels, including two types of 30-year bonds that are due to be paid off by 2056. The expectation is that much of that debt will be paid by media rights agreements and the expected cash generated by the arrival of luxury suites and ticket revenue.
All that can change, however, if the product on the field fails to deliver.Beamer has answered multiple job-security questions over the last few weeks following SEC losses to Mississippi State, Alabama and Kentucky. After Saturday's failure to hold a 17-point lead against the Wildcats, Beamer said he felt like he had the backing of South Carolina's administration."Yeah, I mean, I don't know anything other than what they've told me that they've been super supportive and have been all along," Beamer said.South Carolina athletics director Jeremiah Donati, who did not hire Beamer, took over in 2024 and is continuing his effort to put back together what previous AD Ray Tanner left broken in his wake -- a mix of bad contracts and unfortunate hires. 
Donati voiced support for Beamer during last season's 4-8 slide, but has been quiet thus far in 2026.Lingering financial issuesSouth Carolina paid former football coach Will Muschamp just under $12.9 million in 2020 after his firing, paid former men's basketball coach Frank Martin a $3 million buyout in 2022 and axed recent baseball hire Paul Mainieri after two seasons earlier this spring, which produced a $2.5 million mutual settlement.Mark Kingston was fired as baseball coach during that stretch, too, leaving the Gamecocks treading water with recent managerial decisions.
Current men's basketball coach Lamont Paris, who enters his fifth season this fall, carries around a $12 million buyout -- 65% of his remaining salary -- if fired in the spring. Paris is 62-68 overall with one winning record thus far after he was hired by Tanner as a first-time power conference head coach in March 2022.Tanner stepped down in 2024 to focus on an advisory position he holds through June 2028. He's earning $800,000 over the next two years.As one source put it, the situation's not dissimilar to the conundrum facing Florida State right now, albeit perhaps not as dire given Mike Norvell's gargantuan buyout -- estimated between $47-49 million. His return as coach in 2027 looks more than possible, if not probable, given the savings the Seminoles would make by waiting on a move.
Florida State's also in the middle of an AD search, which heightens the burden of hiring a new football coach while an interim AD is in place. Thanks to a $265 million stadium renovation and another $140 million put toward a football operations building in recent years, Florida State's athletic department closed fiscal year 2025 nearly $450 million in debt -- the second-highest reported total at any public FBS program.That's an easy explanation for why Norvell wasn't fired after last season's struggles in Tallahassee, and it's another example of what many athletic departments are facing as they determine next moves regarding failed coaching hires.At South Carolina, there are issues bigger than Beamer's struggles facing the athletic department right now, and that's why the plug feels far from being pulled -- at least that's the message the university is sending.

title: NFL Week 4 injuries: Updates on Lamar Jackson, Ja'Marr Chase, Saquon Barkley - CBS Sports
description: We assess the latest injury news surrounding Lamar Jackson, Ja'Marr Chase, Saquon Barkley and the other prominent
body:
We assess the latest injury news surrounding Lamar Jackson, Ja'Marr Chase, Saquon Barkley and the other prominent players hurt in Week 4
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:47 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Throughout the first month of the 2026 regular season, we were reminded not once, not twice, but by what felt like an avalanche of injuries sweeping over the league. And it's not just the number of injuries that have popped up over the opening month, but it's also been inflicted on some of the biggest names in the league at the most important positions in the sport. For instance, leading up to Week 4, the NFL had already seen young phenoms like Caleb Williams (hamstring), Jayden Daniels (elbow) and Jaxson Dart (knee) suffer varying degrees of injuries. Meanwhile, Myles Garrett, the defending NFL Defensive Player of the Year and the centerpiece of arguably the biggest trade of the offseason, has yet to play for the Rams on American soil, landing on short-term IR after the opener in Australia due to a knee ailment. Then, there's Baker Mayfield (thumb), Justin Jefferson (ankle), Breece Hall (quad) and De'Von Achane (season-ending ACL tear), among other stars, dealing with injuries as well. It's truly a who's who when they step into the NFL infirmary, and Week 4 only added to that total. Below, we're going to highlight some of the biggest names in the NFL who went down with an injury in Week 4, assess their status, and give them a rating on our panic meter. 
Panic meter barometer: 🔥🔥🔥 = Fears of a season-ender🔥🔥 = Could miss a chunk of time😬😬 = Could miss some time😅 = Should be fineRavens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle)Panic meter: 😅The Ravens quarterback left Sunday's win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury sustained just before halftime and was seen leaving M&T Bank Stadium in a walking boot. While Jackson being in a boot isn't exactly ideal for the two-time NFL MVP, it does sound more like a precaution than anything else. NFL Network reported on Monday morning that Jackson will undergo tests late today, but the initial thought is that he's day-to-day, signaling that the ailment doesn't appear to be too serious. Coach Jesse Minter also said that "there were some talks about that," referring to Jackson possibly reentering the game. The fact that it was a discussion about him going back in (even though he didn't) is another signal that Jackson avoided anything substantial.Week 5 opponent: at Atlanta Falcons Bengals WR Ja'Marr Chase (concussion)Panic meter: 😬😬Chase suffered a concussion in the second quarter of Sunday's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. After making a catch, the wideout was brought to the ground by his facemask by Jaguars corner Jarrian Jones (which drew a penalty), and he was hit again while being taken down. After sitting on the turf for a moment and being evaluated by the training staff, he was taken into the locker room and did not return. Chase is now in the league's concussion protocol, so he'll have to get over several hurdles this week to play next Sunday. Typically, it's a tight turnaround for a player to suffer a concussion and be back the next week, so there's a chance Chase misses at least a week. 
Week 5 opponent: at Miami Dolphins Bengals WR Tee Higgins (adductor)Panic meter: 😬😬Higgins suffered an adductor injury during Cincinnati's final drive of the game after making a leaping catch. He stayed on the field for one snap after being hobbled on the reception before exiting. With this being a soft-tissue injury, it does feel like there's a possibility Higgins could miss some time. That said, there's no definitive word on the severity of the injury yet. Week 5 opponent: at Miami Dolphins Eagles RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring)Panic meter: 😬😬It's been tough sledding for Barkley on the injury front this season. After already dealing with a stinger, the Eagles running back left Sunday's loss to the Rams due to a hamstring injury he suffered in the first quarter. Barkley seemed to pull up after running out of bounds on a carry during Philly's second possession. NFL Network reports that Barkley will undergo testing on Monday, but added that it doesn't appear to be overly serious. That said, as is the case with all soft tissue injuries, they won't know the full extent until they do testing. Week 5 opponent: vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (in London)Eagles CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee)Panic meter: 😬😬The injuries continued to pile up for Philadelphia. On top of Barkley, All-Pro corner Quinyon Mitchell left the game in the third quarter on Sunday due to a knee injury. Mitchell got tangled up on the sideline while tackling Rams running back Blake Corum and appears to have taken a helmet to the knee. NFL Network reports that the hope is Mitchell hyperextended his knee and may have suffered a bone bruise, but testing on Monday will reveal the severity. 
Week 5 opponent: vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (in London)Commanders QB Marcus Mariota (knee)Panic meter: 🔥🔥Mariota has been starting for Washington in place of the injured Jayden Daniels (left elbow), but he couldn't finish Sunday's loss to the Colts in London. The veteran reportedly aggravated his MCL injury and is now undergoing further testing, but he is expected to miss time. There's hope that Daniels will be back next week, but if he's unable to go, it could thrust rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis, who came in under duress for Mariota, into the starter role. Week 5 opponent: vs. New York GiantsBills WR DJ Moore (shoulder)Panic meter: 😬😬Moore aggravated his shoulder injury in Sunday's loss to the Patriots, but ESPN reports that the injury is not considered to be a long-term issue right now. Head coach Joe Brady didn't give an update on Moore's injury postgame. The wideout, who initially injured the shoulder in Week 2 against the Lions,  went down in the second quarter during Sunday's matchup. Before this aggravation, Moore didn't miss any time, but has been limited in practice. He'll have some extra time to recuperate as Buffalo plays on Monday night in Week 5. Week 5 opponent: at Los Angeles RamsPackers LB Edgerrin Cooper (Achilles)Panic meter: 🔥🔥🔥The Packers fear Cooper, their standout linebacker, sustained a torn Achilles in the win over the Buccaneers. Coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged that the injury is "not good" and he'd "suspect" it will be a season-ending injury. 
Week 5 opponent: vs. Chicago BearsChiefs WR Tyquan Thornton (ankle)Panic meter: 🔥🔥🔥The Chiefs receiver was having the game of his life on Sunday against the Raiders, catching five passes for 111 yards and two touchdowns. Unfortunately, he suffered a gruesome ankle injury after making a sensational 55-yard catch and was carted off. Specifically, Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle. They were able to put the ankle back into place, and he did fly back with the team, but he is now out indefinitely. He will undergo an MRI on Monday to see if there is further damage. Week 5 opponent: BYE Chiefs WR Rashee Rice (hamstring)Panic meter: 😅 Head coach Andy Reid said that Rice tweaked his hamstring in the first quarter and did not return. While the wideout did not get back into the game in Week 4, the injury doesn't sound too severe, with NFL Network characterizing it as a very minor hamstring injury. With Kansas City on the bye in Week 5, it appears that Rice may not miss much, if any, time. Week 5 opponent: BYE Broncos CB Patrick Surtain II (ankle)Panic meter: 🔥🔥Denver's star corner is expected to miss time with an ankle injury and will undergo further evaluation on Monday, according to NFL Network. At the time when Surtain went down in the second quarter with a non-contact injury, fears of a season-ender were hard to ignore. However, the injury is not as severe as it initially appeared. Surtian is still expected to be sidelined for a period of time -- NFL Network floated a couple of weeks or an IR stint -- but it is not expected to be season-ending, which is good news for the Broncos. 
Week 5 opponent: at Los Angeles ChargersChargers OT Rashawn Slater (ankle)Panic meter: 🔥🔥Rashawn Slater left Los Angeles' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks in the fourth quarter due to an ankle injury and did not return. NFL Network reports that the Chargers' star left tackle is believed to have suffered a high ankle sprain based on initial exams. He's slated to undergo an MRI, but this is the type of injury that could leave a player out for several weeks and possibly place them on short-term IR. Week 5 opponent: vs. Denver BroncosBears QB Caleb Williams (hamstring)Panic meter: 😬😬 Chicago will continue to be without Caleb Williams as the former No. 1 overall pick recovers from a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 2 against Minnesota. Head coach Ben Johnson announced on Monday that backup Tyson Bagent is expected to get the start in Week 5, ruling Williams out for another week. The Bears did not elect to place Williams on injured reserve, leaving the door open for him to return at any time. However, with him out on Sunday against Green Bay, that would be the third straight game he's missed, with Week 6 at Atlanta as the next possible window for him to make his return.  Week 5 opponent: at Green Bay Packers

title: Mike Vrabel responds to C.J. Gardner-Johnson's criticism of Patriots WR Efton Chism III - CBS Sports

body:
Gardner-Johnson called Chism a 'practice squad player' and suggested the Patriots receiver could not replicate his spectacular game-winning catch
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:38 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New England Patriots upset the Buffalo Bills in a key early-season divisional showdown on Sunday and got over the top in the close battle with help from an unlikely source. Wide receiver Efton Chism III secured the game-winning touchdown in the Patriots' 29-26 victory on the biggest play of his young career: A diving, one-handed catch in the end zone with 1:50 to play.Bills cornerback C.J. Gardner-Johnson brushed off the highlight reception as a fluke. He called Chism a "practice squad player" and said that if the teams were to run that play over again, the wide receiver would not be able to replicate his stellar catch. It should be noted that Chism has been on the Patriots' 53-man roster since signing as an undrafted free agent in 2025."We're not going to get into no bulletin board material," Gardner-Johnson said postgame before promptly giving the Patriots plenty of bulletin board material. "An elevated guy made a hell of a catch. Probably won't hear from him again, respectfully. I say that with a lot of confidence, because it's like, he didn't put his confidence in his best player. If that was it, he would've threw it to Doubs or somebody. They won the game. Whatever. They ain't do s--- better than us. We gotta play better."Patriots coach Mike Vrabel came to Chism's defense with his reaction to Gardner-Johnson's jab. He had a day to concoct the perfect response and delivered it Monday on his weekly radio appearance on WEEI.
"For a guy that's been on eight teams in four years? I guess he knows the drill," Vrabel said of the Bills defender. (For the record, Gardner-Johnson has been with seven teams in his eight-year NFL career, including spending time on the Bears and Ravens practice squads). New England, for now, has the last laugh thanks to its coach's "mic drop" of a reply. The teams will meet again in Week 13, and Chism will have an opportunity to show Gardner-Johnson that he, in fact, can replicate the dazzling catch.
Chism is a second-year professional out of Eastern Washington, where he broke Cooper Kupp's school record for single-season receptions and earned FCS first-team All-American honors as a senior. The Patriots were one of multiple teams to target him as an undrafted free agent, and they kept him around on their active roster following an impressive rookie preseason. Chism made only a couple of appearances in 2025 but displayed his potential in Week 17 when he hauled in his first two career receptions.
With No. 1 receiver A.J. Brown out due to a high ankle sprain, Chism saw action in each of the last three games and made one start. He has four catches on the year for 41 yards and the highlight-reel touchdown.

body:
With the defense bottoming out in 2026, Campbell needs to make changes in order to take his team back to the championship conversation
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:09 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Pull a random defensive statistic out of a hat, and there is a solid chance the Detroit Lions rank dead last in the NFL in that metric. Through Week 4, no team surrendered more points or yards than the Lions. This is now the second consecutive year in which Detroit's defense has been a liability, yet coach Dan Campbell is hesitant to make any significant changes to the unit's structure or leadership.Following the 32-26 loss to the Carolina Panthers on "Sunday Night Football," Campbell admitted that the defense is a glaring issue. But instead of firing second-year coordinator Kelvin Sheppard, shaking up the play-calling duties or doing anything else to reconstruct the defense's framework, Campbell said he wants to "exhaust everything" with the players and coaches he has by his side."I'm not talking about all that," Campbell said after the game of a potential leadership change. "I'm talking about getting better right now with what we've got. That's what we're going to do. We're going to find a way to get better with what we've got. There are other things that we can do. We've tweaked a little bit every week here. There's still some things that we can try that we haven't yet to try to settle some things down and see if we can help. It's a work in progress."None of the adjustments Campbell and his staff have made on the fly over the last year have produced the desired results. Sunday night was just the latest example. Carolina quarterback Bryce Young entered the game as the NFL's leading passer and only padded his advantage over the rest of the league's signal-callers with a 329-yard outing. Wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan enjoyed a career night with 14 catches, 192 yards and two touchdowns. On the ground, Chuba Hubbard racked up 122 yards and a pair of scores.
With each passing week, Detroit shows that no matter how excellent its offense may be, it is always in grave danger of losing. The Panthers, New York Jets, Buffalo Bills and New Orleans Saints each posted at least 24 points against this team. New Orleans tallied 30 in the second half and overtime of the season opener. Still, Campbell and his players stand up for Sheppard.
In Sheppard's defense, his personnel is less than fully stocked. The absences of Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch from the safety unit, plus Terrion Arnold's late-offseason departure, are undoubtedly key reasons why the Lions' secondary cannot get off the field. But the front is still full of Pro Bowl talent like Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell.The issues date back to before those defensive backfield personnel deficiencies, so it is clear that the troubles go much deeper.
Defensive downturn under Kelvin SheppardDetroit has not been a defensive juggernaut at any point during the Campbell era, but there was a brief period at the height of his tenure where the Lions were nearly as effective at preventing opponents from scoring as they were at putting points on the board themselves. Former defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn built the group from the ground up and turned it into a top-10 unit before his departure to take the Jets' head coaching job.Since then, it has been nothing but regression. The team as a whole suffered in turn. During Glenn's tenure, the Lions improved their win total every year. In his final season, they went 15-2 and reached the divisional round of the playoffs. Once Sheppard took over, Detroit instantly regressed to 9-8 and missed the postseason, and it is off to a mediocre start to 2026.SeasonCoordinatorScoring defense rankYards allowed rankExpected points rank2024Aaron Glenn720102025Kelvin Sheppard2218182026Kelvin Sheppard323232Lions wasting their Super Bowl windowThe Lions' offense is championship material. A few of the best players in the NFL at their respective positions reside on this unit. Jahmyr Gibbs is perhaps the top running back in the league. Penei Sewell might be the league's most elite tackle. Amon-Ra St. Brown is a top-flight wide receiver. Sam LaPorta is off to a tremendous start to his career at tight end. Holding the unit together is a commendable quarterback in Jared Goff, who logged the seventh 400-yard game of his career and the third of his Lions tenure in Week 4.Winning shootouts is not a sustainable model, though. That was evident a year ago when the Lions finished just one game above .500. It is clear in 2026 as they open the campaign at 2-2. The offense can keep pace with nearly anyone, but the group on the other side of the ball is putting too much of the burden on Goff and his supporting cast.There is foundational talent on the defense, too. Hutchinson and Campbell are the kinds of pieces that can anchor a formidable group. They just need more help on the back end and a play-caller who utilizes them more effectively.Unless the Lions shake up their defensive leadership or make a splash personnel move, the group will continue to weigh down a team that, for so many reasons, should be in the Super Bowl conversation.

body:
Hello football friends, and welcome to the Monday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!First, I'd like to apologize. The NFL had its first Cat Bowl on Sunday, and I didn't mention it a single time in either of last week's newsletters. The internet was basically invented for three things and one of them is talking about cats, so I fumbled the ball here. Anyway, Week 4 marked the first time in NFL history that the four cat teams faced off on the same day:The Panthers beat the LionsThe Jaguars beat the BengalsI'm now rooting for an all-cat Super Bowl, and if that happens, I promise I will give you all the cat information you can handle in the lead-up to the game. Unfortunately, we are NOT going to be talking anymore about cats in today's newsletter, but we do have a lot to cover, so let's get to the rundown. As always, here's your daily reminder to tell all your friends to sign up for the newsletter. To get them signed up, just click here.  
1. NFL Week 4 grades: Patriots earn high mark for win at Highmark, Chiefs and Raiders get same grade
                                                                    Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images
                                                            There were 16 games on the schedule in Week 4. I graded them all. I'm only pointing that out because this will be the last time for several weeks that we'll get a full 16-game slate. We're getting into "bye" season and that will be starting in Week 5 with the Chiefs and Panthers getting the week off. The Chiefs' final game before their bye was a wild one over the Raiders, and that's where we're going to start our grades today. Chiefs 30-27 over RaidersChiefs takeaway: At the rate things are going, the offseason signing of Kenneth Walker might go down as one of the best free agency acquisitions in NFL history. In a game where Patrick Mahomes struggled with his accuracy, the Chiefs' offense was able to chug along thanks to Walker, who rushed for 177 yards and two touchdowns. When you're outshining Mahomes, you're doing something right in Kansas City. Tyquan Thornton had a breakout game for the Chiefs, but he might not see the field again this year after suffering a gruesome injury.  Andy Reid probably won't be thrilled with the overall performance of his defense -- they had zero sacks for the third straight game and struggled to stop the Raiders' big tight ends -- but Xavier Nwankpa did save the day with a game-clinching interception. It's hard to complain about anything when you're undefeated and that's what the Chiefs are. Grade: BRaiders takeaway: It's been a long time since the Raiders have been in a game like this and that seemed to show in crunch. The Raiders made mistake after mistake in the fourth quarter, which overshadowed an otherwise impressive game. DarekeYoung had a back-breaking fumble on a kickoff return that allowed the Chiefs to take a two-score lead. The Raiders defense did a good job of holding the Chiefs' offense in check until the fourth quarter, when the wheels fell off the wagon. And let's not forget about Kirk Cousins, who threw for 365 yards: He's doing his best to make sure Fernando Mendoza never sees the field this year. The Raiders didn't get the result they wanted, but they certainly proved that they can play with anyone. It won't be surprising at all if this team is competing for a playoff spot come January. Grade: BPatriots 29-26 over BillsPatriots takeaway: After struggling through the first three weeks, Drake Maye proved that he can still play at a high level. The Patriots QB needed a big game, and he got it: Not only did he throw for 269 yards and three touchdowns, but he also rushed for a team-high 54 yards. Maye also deserves a lot of credit for engineering a game-winning 73-yard TD drive that saw him complete four passes of at least 12 yards, including a 23-yard score on a WILD catch by Efton Chism that ended up providing the game-winning points. Maye wasn't perfect - there were still too many turnovers - but if he continues playing this well, the Patriots will be in the playoff conversation later in the season. Grade: A-Bills takeaway: It's hard for the Bills' offense to win when it's not on the field, and that was one of the problems for Buffalo in this game. The Bills had only four possessions lasting at least five plays, and on top of that, they couldn't get their run game going. The Bills entered this game with the third-best rushing offense in the NFL, and they faced a Patriots defense that has struggled to stop the run this year. Despite that, Joe Brady decided to run the ball just 12 times with James Cook. That was bad, but the defense was the bigger problem. The Bills suddenly don't look so invincible. Grade: B-As for the other 26 grades that we handed out so far in Week 4, you can check those out by clicking here. 



    2. NFL Week 4 winners and losers: Eagles third-down offense hits rock bottom You can't have a week of NFL action without having winners and losers, so we have some winners and losers. Carter Bahns came up with this week's list, and we're going to check out his losers below. At the top of our losers' list is an Eagles offense that looks like it's falling apart. LOSERS Eagles third-down offense. The Philadelphia Eagles made the wrong kind of franchise history in Week 4 with the worst third-down execution in their 94 years of existence. Never before had the offense gone 0-12 in third-down situations until Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Making matters worse, the Eagles found it difficult to move the chains on fourth down, too, with just one conversion on four tries. Those three turnovers on downs were costly. First-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion was always going to be heavily scrutinized this season because of the high-pressure situation he walked into. Sunday's performance was no resounding endorsement of his scheme nor his play-calling abilities.Commanders QB situation. Fans in London did not have much reason to cheer for the Commanders in Sunday's international game. The Colts pulled away from them in a 30-13 rout at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and did so comfortably as it was clear the Commanders would not be able to maintain pace once Marcus Mariota went down with a game-ending knee injury. Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, out of Rutgers, stepped into action and completed just 15 of 33 passes with a touchdown and an interception in his professional regular-season debut. Moving forward, the Commanders will either have a backup quarterback on the field or a less-than-healthy Jayden Daniels. There is no telling how effective he will be when he comes back from his elbow injury, which will require offseason surgery and which forces him to play with a brace on his non-throwing arm. Texans. Defense was supposed to be Houston's calling card this year. It certainly was not on Sunday when it surrendered three touchdowns to Javonte Williams in the second half alone and had no answers for CeeDee Lamb. Houston should finally grab its first win of the campaign next week when it meets the Tennessee Titans in a matchup of two winless AFC South teams. It might, however, already be too late to save a disastrous start to the year.If you want to see Carter's list of winners (and a couple of other losers), be sure to click here. 3. Overreactions from Week 4: Will the Cowboys take the NFC East?
                                                                    Alex Slitz/Getty Images
                                                            Everyone on the internet loves to overreact to things, and that's especially true when we're talking about the NFL. Personally, I overreact to everything. With that in mind, Zach Pereles decided to take a look at several things that happened during Week 4 to decide if we're all overreacting.  
Statement: The Rams shouldn't be Super Bowl favorites.Overreaction or reality: Overreaction. There are two ways to view the Rams' 24-20 win over the injury-ravaged Eagles: "Wow, that was super unimpressive" or "Wow, that was an impressive comeback." It can be both. Los Angeles struggling to beat a Philadelphia team without DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Quinyon Mitchell, Zack Baun, Lane Johnson, Landon Dickerson and others was a bad look ... for 52-plus minutes. The score will lie about who dominated this game. The Rams had 415 yards of offense and averaged 5.4 yards per play, compared to 172 yards and 3.0 yards per play for Philadelphia. The Rams committed some horrible turnovers and penalties, but on a play-by-play basis, they were far superior. This was a crucial, crucial win, and one that should only prove Los Angeles can win when so much goes wrong.Statement: The Cowboys will win the NFC East.Overreaction or reality: Reality. Speaking of important wins, the Cowboys just got their most important since the 2023 season: Dallas 34, Houston 30. This is a game the Cowboys needed to win, and they found a way to do so. Looking around the division, the Eagles' offense remains a mess, the Giants are 3-1 but not likely to threaten with Jameis Winston under center, and the Commanders are in a world of trouble.  Simply put, Dallas, with a defense that should only improve and an offense that can go toe-to-toe with any, should win this division.Statement: Ben Johnson will win Coach of the Year. Overreaction or reality: Overreaction. Ben Johnson should be the frontrunner for Coach of the Year. He's now won games with Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum ... and it's only Week 4! According to CBS Sports research, only one other team has had three different quarterbacks throw for 200+ yards in a win through four weeks: the 1997 Jaguars.  Unfortunately for Johnson's Coach of the Year candidacy, the award tends to go to a coach whose team way overachieves. Basically, the external preseason expectations were likely too high for Johnson and the Bears for him to win the award this year, even if you could argue he's been the best coach in the sport so far. 
There are plenty more overreactions and you can check them out here.
    
    

    4. Eleven crazy stats from Week 4: Vikings set football back 100 yearsEvery Sunday night, I get an email from our research department here at CBS Sports, and every Sunday, that email always includes some crazy stats about the games that were just played. With that in mind, here are 11 crazy stats from Week 4: Vikings are doing the impossible. The Vikings didn't score a touchdown in their 15-10 win over the Dolphins, which means they've now won two games this season without scoring a touchdown. That makes Minnesota the first team in more than 100 years to start 4-0 by winning two or more games without a TD. The only other two teams to pull that off were the 1922 and 1923 Chicago Cardinals. High drama over the past two weeks. There have been 23 games decided by one score over the past two weeks, which is tied for the most in any two-week span in NFL history (Weeks 1-2, 2013). If we get a one-score game tonight between the Saints and Falcons, then the NFL will set a record for the number of one-score games over a two-week span. The Jets finally get an interception. Last year, the Jets became the first team in NFL history to go an entire season without recording an interception. Well, that drought is finally over. Minkah Fitzpatrick picked off Bears' QB Tyson Bagent on Sunday to give the Jets their first interception in 637 days. Brock Purdy is unsackable. The 49ers QB still hasn't taken a sack through four games, marking just the third time in NFL history that the QB of a 4-0 team made it through the first four weeks without being sacked. Purdy joins Dan Marino from the 1984 Dolphins and Peyton Manning from the 2005 Colts. Both of those teams finished 14-2, which would seem to be a good sign for San Francisco.   Texans just made history, but not in a good way. The Texans just became the first team in NFL history to hit 0-4 without throwing an interception during the first four weeks. The Texans are also the first team since the 2012 Saints to fall to 0-4 just one season after winning at least 12 games.    Rams pull off the impossible. In Jalen Hurts' career, he had never lost a game (41-0) when leading by 10 points or more in the final five minutes, but that streak is now over. Against the Rams, the Eagles were up 20-10 with four minutes left before blowing the lead in a 24-20 loss. This win marked the first time in Matthew Stafford's Rams' career that he overcame a double-digit deficit in the final five minutes. He's now 1-18 in that situation following the win.  Jets looked like an expansion team. During Chicago's 23-12 win over the Jets, the Bears had more first downs (34) than the Jets had total plays (32). This marked the first time this century that we've seen this happen. The last time this situation came up was when the expansion Browns came back to the NFL in 1999. In their Week 1 opener, the Steelers put up 33 first downs compared to just 27 plays for the Browns. That's the only other time this has happened in the Super Bowl era. Chicks dig the long ball. With one game left to be played, there have been 16 field goals of at least 50 years in Week 4, which is the fourth-highest number for any week in NFL history. If the Falcons and Saints combine for four kicks of 50 yards or more tonight, that would move Week 4 to the second-highest total all time (the record is 21, set in Week 1 of the 2024 season). Kenneth Walker is running over everyone. The Chiefs running back had 177 rushing yards against the Raiders and he now has at least 175 yards scrimmage yards in four games with the Chiefs. That makes him just the second player in NFL history to top 175 yards from scrimmage in three of his first four games with a new team, joining Billy Sims, who did it with the Lions in 1980. Golden Lamb. In the Cowboys' win over the Texans, CeeDee Lamb had 17 catches for 189 yards and a TD. His total gave him the most receptions in NFL history by a player who also caught a game-winning TD in the final two minutes. He also became the fourth player in NFL history with at least 17 receptions, 185 receiving yards and a touchdown reception in a single game, joining Rams WR Tom Fears (1950), 49ers WR Terrell Owens (2000) and Broncos WR Brandon Marshall (2009). Refs get flag happy.  There were a total of 11 teams called for at least 10 penalties and the ugliest game for the was Chargers-Seahawks. The two teams got flagged a combined total of 30 times for 280 yards. The 30 penalties were the most in an NFL game since 2003. If you see any other fun facts, feel free to tweet them at me. 5. Monday night preview: Picks and best bets for Falcons at Saints
                                                                    Todd Kirkland/Getty Images
                                                            Twenty years ago, the SuperDome reopened after Hurricane Katrina with a Monday night game between the Falcons and Saints. The NFL is celebrating the anniversary by having the two teams go at it again tonight. This game will come with some high stakes because the winner will move into a first-place tie with the Panthers in the NFC South. 
Here's one reason why each team should be feeling confident going into the game: Why the Falcons can win: Through the first three weeks of the season, the Saints have given up the sixth-most rushing yards in the NFL this year. The good news for the Falcons is that they have the perfect guy to take advantage of that: Bijan Robinson. If Robinson gets going, that will set up the Falcons offense for success. That will take a lot of pressure off of Michael Penix, which means a solid game by Robinson could also open up the passing game, which is exactly what happened during Atlanta's 35-14 win over the Packers' in Week 3. Why the Saints can win: The Falcons haven't been able to stop the pass, which should make this game interesting. Through the first three weeks of the season, the Falcons have surrendered the fourth-most passing yards in the NFL and the Saints just happen to have the perfect guy to take advantage of that: Tyler Shough. The second-year QB is averaging 305.7 passing yards per game, which ranks third in the NFL. Even if Shough has a big game, there is one thing he needs to avoid and that's turning the ball over. In his two-year career, the Saints are 1-7 when Shough throws at least one interception, but 4-1 when he doesn't. You can get a full preview of the game from Jared Dubin by clicking here.If you're thinking about betting on the game, here are a couple of props. ONE RUSHING PROP I LIKE: Drake London OVER 75.5 receiving yards (-115 at BetMGM): The Falcons receiver has gone over 100 YARDS in six of the past seven games that he's played with Michael Penix at QB. And that includes the Falcons' Week 3 win that saw London go off for 194 yards. The Saints defense will likely be focused on slowing down Bijan Robinson, so that could set up London to have a big day. ONE KICKING PROP I LIKE: Nick Folk OVER 1.5 field goals (-135 at FanDuel: The Falcons kicker has made at least two field goals in two of his first three games and that would be three of three if he didn't miss a field goal in Week 2. Also, Kevin Stefanski isn't shy about taking the points, so that should certainly help Folk hit the over here .  If you're wondering how my props are doing this year, I'm 5-9 (2-5 on kicker props and 3-4 on all other props). After starting off 5-3, I'm not 0-6 on my last six props. This is clearly a sign that you should do the opposite of whatever I predict. And now, it's time for some picks. PICKS FOR 'MNF'Jared Dubin's pick: Saints 28-20 over FalconsJordan Dajani's pick: Saints 23-20 over FalconsJohn Breech's pick: Falcons 26-23 over SaintsTyler Sullivan's pick: Falcons 26-24 over SaintsPrisco's pick: Falcons 33-30 over Saints
Over on our CBSSports.com picks page, our seven experts are split with four taking the Falcons to win and three taking the Saints. 
    
	

    6. Extra points: Lamar Jackson headlines ugly Sunday for injuriesIt's been a busy few days around the NFL, and since it's nearly impossible to keep track of everything, I put together a quick roundup for you.Lamar Jackson dealing with ankle injury. The Ravens QB didn't play during the second half of Baltimore's 24-18 win over the Titans after injuring his ankle. After the game, Jackson left the stadium wearing a protective boot. Jackson will be undergoing an MRI today to determine the severity of the injury. If he has to miss any time, then Tyler Huntley will be the starter in Baltimore. Bengals receiving stars both dealing with injuries. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) both left the game on Sunday due to their injury. If those guys can't go in Week 5, that means the Bengals will be extremely short-handed for their game against the Dolphins. It's hard to see Chase missing more than one game, if he misses any at all, but if Higgins' injury is serious, he could miss several weeks. Chiefs eyeing possible reunion with Tyreek Hill. With injuries piling up at receiver, it appears that the Chiefs are going to look into a possible reunion with Hill.  During the Chiefs' win over the Raiders on Sunday, Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton both left the game with an injury (Thornton suffered a gruesome leg injury). The Argentinian legend will play his last ever match with the national team on October 6 against Benin

        The day has come. On Tuesday, October 6, Lionel Messi will play his last ever match in an Argentina jersey, and it's hard to even begin to wrap your brain around the end of one of the most incredible soccer legacies in the history of the sport. After winning the 2022 World Cup, Messi achieved the last milestone his career was missing and changed his legacy with the national team he represented since 2005, when he made his name known in the world at the 2005 Under-20 World Cup. Then he stuck around for four more years and finished second in 2026 just for good measure. Since he made his debut with Argentina and with Barcelona in Spain, Messi was considered one of the most promising talents around, but being from Argentina also meant that he faced eternal comparison with the legend of legends, Diego Armando Maradona. Despite winning everything he could with Barcelona, his first decade with the Argentinian national team was challenging and ultimately led to his initial decision to retire from the national team after losing two Copa America finals in a row in 2015 and 2016. The ongoing comparison with his idol definitely touched him, as he couldn't bring the same joy that Maradona brought to the millions of Argentinian fans in 1986, when Argentina won the World Cup in Mexico. Eventually, his nation coaxed him back, and by 2021 things started to change for the better. Messi won his first-ever Copa America, followed by the success of the 2022 World Cup. 
        
            
                Lionel Messi's Argentina career timeline: Two retirements, years of struggle and redemption at 2022 World Cup
                
                    Francesco Porzio                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
In that World Cup, Messi scored seven goals, won the World Cup, and was named player of the tournament before also winning his last Ballon d'Or in 2023. In 2024, he won another Copa America, beating Colombia in the final, marking one of the greatest cycles in the history of Argentinian soccer. Amazingly that run was almost topped with the 2026 World Cup, but Argentina lost in the final to Spain. Only a few weeks after the defeat in the final, Messi announced his retirement, which followed the news of the death of his father, Jorge. 
Chasing Maradona: Argentina's one-of-a-kind icon From the moment Messi debuted, there was always a comparison with his idol and the most iconic Argentine player in history, Maradona. Would Messi become the new Maradona? That was the question everyone seemed to be asking, a question that quickly evolved into a bigger one: Is Messi better than Maradona? The debate only intensified after Messi led Argentina to World Cup glory in 2022, and it's still a topic today, and probably will be for a long time. Before answering that question, we should reflect on what Maradona meant for Argentina in the 1980's. Maradona embodied the soccer player's mentality of those years, and was an unapologetic public figure, no small thing given the political context of those years. Argentina were emerging from a period of dictatorship that lasted from 1976 to 1983, years where thousands of Argentinians had to face the challenges of the military government, and thousands of them were killed as well. It all changed in 1982, when Argentina's defeat in the Falklands War led to the collapse of the military dictatorship that had ruled the country. The junta, regarded as one of the most brutal regimes in Latin American history, waged the so-called "Dirty War" against suspected opponents. The military surrendered power in 1983 and Argentina returned to democracy.Maradona's exploits at the 1986 World Cup, especially in the quarterfinal against England, in the "Hand of God" match when Maradona scored the opening goal with his hand, followed by the "Goal of the Century" were seen as a political act, more than a soccer game. Maradona was perfect to embody that role model for the fans, and when he was suspended at the 1994 World Cup after failing to pass a drug test, the whole country backed him. He was a national hero, more than a soccer player, and he did something similar at Napoli where he played from 1984 to 1991, winning the first two Serie A titles in the history of the club. The fans were so devoted to him that, during the 1990 World Cup semifinals between Italy and Argentina in Naples, where the stadium is now named after Maradona, the majority of the home crowd cheered for him.
The man was more than a football player for Argentina, he was a national hero, and that was what Messi was always compared to. Why Messi is different Maradona met Messi multiple times and seemed to be happy about him becoming a popular player among the younger generations. When Messi made his World Cup debut in 2006 with Argentina, Maradona was in the crowd cheering him and smiling. Four years later, at the 2010 World Cup with Maradona as coach, Messi failed to score a single goal as Argentina were eliminated by Germany in the quarterfinals, suffering a heavy 4–0 defeat. The result also brought an end to Maradona's tenure as national team coach. A partnership that, sadly, didn't work out. 
Messi has a completely different personality on and off the pitch to the one of Maradona, and whereas Maradona was larger than life. Messi's life has been, to all appearances, entirely devoted to the sport. Consequently, he has been judged only by his results on the pitch. This is why, when things were not working at all between him and the national team, he was criticised wildly, and probably too much. He was simply dependent on the results, so by 2022, with Messi already 35 and seemingly past his prime, the comparison seemed pretty much settled. Then he started to win. Trophy after trophy, the 2022 World Cup finally brought a sense of relief for Messi. Sadly, Maradona was not able to witness another triumph for his beloved national team, as he had passed away two years earlier.
Though, despite their differences, there is one point of cominality in their career. During the summer of 2020, Messi gave an interview to La Sexta anticipated about the possibility of leaving Barcelona at the end of the 2020-2021 season, something that did eventually come to pass, despite his desire to stay. Just as Maradona left Napoli overnight without ever having the chance to say goodbye to his fans, Messi found himself in the same situation. They both left the clubs they loved the most, without a proper farewell. On Tuesday the Argentinian national team will make sure that won't be the case again. Ultimately though, as Messi rides off into the sunset, it's impossible to say who was better between the two, but there is one thing that is certain. Lionel Messi wasn't the new Maradona. He won on his own terms, leaving his mark on the history of the game.

Towns expected a contract to be quickly worked out easily after his playoff showcase, but it's now clear that will not come before the season begins

        Karl-Anthony Towns was on top of the world this summer after helping deliver New York its first NBA title in more than 50 years. The New Jersey native was sensational in the playoffs and assumed that performance would make it pretty easy to negotiate a deal this summer to remain with the Knicks long-term. With the start of the 2026-27 season on the horizon, that has proved not to be the case and the Knicks' star big man offered a disappointing update on extension talks on Monday ahead of New York's preseason opener in Philly. "It don't look good," said Towns of getting an extension done before the season, per The Athletic. "... Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me. None of those things have come close to happening." The Knicks face the same dilemma that many recent championship teams have: under the current collective bargaining agreement and the second-apron restrictions, it is extremely difficult to retain top talent and keep a championship core intact. To be clear, this is a problem of the NBA's own construction, as the aprons were fought for by the owners and (many would argue, foolishly) without strong enough pushback from the players' association. 
Knicks owner James Dolan was quick to rain on their championship celebration by making it clear he would not dare cross the second apron, drawing a hard line in the sand about how far he was willing to go to keep this team intact. What makes the Towns extension saga particularly fascinating is the fact that he said he'd be willing to take less than the max, much like Jalen Brunson did to help build this roster in the first place. Towns noted he wants to work out a deal that helps keep the team together, but he also knows this could be one of his final major deals and has to find that balance between still getting something close to his top value. His comments on Monday indicate the Knicks are not meeting him in the middle to his liking, and according to the New York Post, the Knicks' current offer is for $200 million over four years -- nearly $77 million below the max they could offer. 
That would be a massive discount for Towns to accept; the result is a stalemate.The Knicks have other extensions to worry about in the next 12 months, with Josh Hart also extension-eligible this summer and then OG Anunoby and Jalen Brunson up for new deals in 2027. The Towns negotiations, as much as anything, feel like a message to the entire roster about how the Knicks will approach those talks and what they expect players to sacrifice if they want to keep this core together. Negotiations can continue into the season, but most players like to avoid contract talks while they're playing, which could create some real stress in New York. For one, a star in a contract standoff is not exactly the best mental state to get Towns playing loose and free. From there, there are real questions about how the Knicks' front office would handle the situation. Would the Knicks be willing to table negotiations and wait until next summer, when Towns can become a free agent (should he decline his player option) and risk the possibility of him walking for nothing? Would they (again) explore trade opportunities for Towns, knowing he could walk if they feel like the max offer they're willing to present is below what he's willing to take? 
In most situations, you'd expect the team and its second-best player on a championship squad to be able to find some sort of compromise -- especially if the player is willing to take less than the max, which he would be more than within his rights to demand. But Knicks ownership is something of a wild card in the sense that Dolan has never been one to feel the need to appease fans. If Towns walks next summer, Knicks fans would be furious, but that has been the default setting for Knicks fans towards the team for so long that Dolan simply may not care.
